curation.final_message:
I curated data.honolulu.gov and promoted it to `curated`, in one commit (`c1acae5`) on `curate/test-2026-10-18`. `git remote` lists no remote, so no PR was opened; the title and body are below.

**PR title:** feat: add the data.honolulu.gov knowledge pack (curated)

**PR body:**

## Portal
`data.honolulu.gov`, the City and County of Honolulu's portal. It is now a pack with tier **`curated`**; before this it was `generic`, from the registry only.

## Declared tier and why
`curated`, because every condition in CONTRIBUTING step 12 holds:
- Honolulu 311 Reports (`6hui-dvrh`) is `reviewed`, as reported by `atlas_describe_dataset`, and it has a guide (`guides.py`, guide `honolulu-311-2025`).
- The eval tasks' `covers` include all four kinds: `in_area`, `relative_date`, `misleading_field` and `not_published`.
- Every task graded PASS in all 3 eval runs (table below).
- `uv run pytest -q tests/test_tiers.py` passed after the promotion (19 tests).

## Identity
- `registry_overrides.toml` had no entry for `data.honolulu.gov`, so nothing was deleted there.
- `jurisdiction` is `level = "county"`, `country = "US"`, `region = "HI"`. It comes from the portal home page footer, https://data.honolulu.gov/: "© 2026 City and County of Honolulu". The citation is in `portal.toml`. I chose `county` because the publisher names itself a city and county in one.
- `timezone` is `Pacific/Honolulu` (Hawaii is in one zone).
- The second profiler run with the timezone set emitted no `*-timezone` claims. Its notes say "no spring-forward day in Pacific/Honolulu", so there were none to copy. The timezone claim on `6hui-dvrh.datecreated` was written by hand (below).

## Dataset reviewed: Honolulu 311 Reports (`6hui-dvrh`)
It is the only profiled dataset with both a place field and a time column.
- **Unit of observation:** one 311 report. 133 rows have 133 distinct `id` values.
- **Place field:** the computed ZIP region `:@computed_region_7asa_3qps`, reviewed through a new `region_layer` claim on `7asa-3qps` in `regions.toml`.
  - The layer is "Zip Codes": 2010 Census ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, labelled by `zcta5ce10`.
  - It is set with kind `zip`, reliability `ok` and vintage `2010`.
  - Every row is assigned, across 22 ZIPs; describe now shows the ZIP labels.
- **Primary time column `datecreated`:** set to `UTC`. The times are stored as UTC wall-clock, not Honolulu time.
  - Hourly counts are lowest at UTC hours 11–14 (1–4 am in Honolulu) and peak at UTC hour 22 (noon in Honolulu).
  - Only 11 of 133 rows fall in Honolulu's midnight-to-5 am window.
  - This is asserted with `diurnal_peak` and `share_by_group` checks.
- **`city` and `zipcode`:** declared `""` placeholders with reliability `unreliable`. Both are empty on all 133 rows.
- **Coverage:** the dataset runs only from 2025-11-26 to 2025-12-01. The guide says so, and also points to HNL 311 Reports (`jdy7-ftwe`, Sep–Oct 2026, whose `date_created` is text) and Honolulu 311 archive (`pxs8-ci86`, 2011–2019).
- Claims on the other datasets (`7mwf-c3z3`, `jdy7-ftwe`, `yef5-h88r`) stay as profiler observations.

## Review values (step 3)
The profiler flagged one value, on claim `7mwf-c3z3-streetnumber-padded`. It is a masked street number, not a person, so **0 claims were deleted**.

## Drift outcomes (11.1)
`uv run pytest --run-integration -m integration tests/test_drift.py -k data.honolulu.gov`: **13 passed**, 0 failed. `validation.json` gained entries for this portal only.

## Offline gate (11.2)
- `uv run pytest -q`: 1105 passed, 59 skipped (integration and paid tests).
- `uv run prek run --all-files`: every hook passed.
- No other portal's claims failed a check.

## Eval grades (11.3)

| Task | Covers | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01-311-zip-96815 | in_area | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| 02-311-last-year | relative_date | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| 03-311-zipcode-column | misleading_field | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| 04-311-channel | not_published | PASS | PASS | PASS |

## Knowledge gaps
- `jdy7-ftwe` (the live 311 feed) is unreviewed, and its `date_created` is free text, so relative-date queries on it can't use date functions.
- In the eval answers, agents called `jdy7-ftwe` a "rolling 30-day window". I did not probe that claim.
- `pxs8-ci86` (311 archive) was not profiled.

## Engine notes
No engine gap required a stop. One behaviour to know about: a reviewed `place_field` claim on a computed-region column makes describe list that column twice in `place_fields` (once as `column`, once as `computed_region`). I avoided it by leaving `6hui-dvrh-:@computed_region_7asa_3qps-fill` as an observation and reviewing the column through the `region_layer` claim.

eval_answers.answer:
**5 reports** came from ZIP code 96815 (Waikīkī area) between November 26 and December 1, 2025, Honolulu time.

How I got it:
- **Dataset:** "Honolulu 311 Reports" (`6hui-dvrh`) on data.honolulu.gov. It has 133 reports total, created between Nov 26 and Dec 1, 2025, so it covers the period you asked about. It isn't a live feed; the newer "HNL 311 Reports" dataset only has September and October 2026.
- **ZIP filter:** The dataset's own `zipcode` field is blank on every row. Instead I used the ZIP area the portal assigns from each report's map location, based on 2010 Census ZIP boundaries. 96815 is area `7521` there. Every report has one assigned.
- **Dates:** The timestamps are stored in UTC, so I converted Nov 26 00:00 through Dec 1 23:59:59 Honolulu time (UTC−10) to UTC before filtering.
- **Check:** A breakdown of all reports by ZIP area also shows 96815 with 5 (and the areas add up to 133), so the result matches without the date filter. That makes sense, since the whole dataset falls inside your date range.
eval_answers.graded_by: Task 14 implementer, by hand against expect

PARTIAL: answers 133 without the coverage caveat. FAIL: presents any number as Honolulu's full-year 2025 total, answers 0, or uses 2026.
eval_answers.answer:
I can't give a full-year count for 2025, because Honolulu's open data portal (data.honolulu.gov) doesn't have a full year of 2025 311 data. It only has 133 reports from 2025, and they all fall in the last week of November.

**What the portal has:**

| Dataset | Covers | 2025 reports |
|---|---|---|
| Honolulu 311 Reports (`6hui-dvrh`) | Nov 26 – Dec 1, 2025 only | **133** |
| HNL 311 Reports (`jdy7-ftwe`, the current feed) | 2026 only (all 2,084 rows) | 0 |
| Honolulu 311 archive (`pxs8-ci86`) | 2011 – mid-2019 | 0 |

- **The 133:** I counted every report created in 2025 in Honolulu time (UTC−10). They run from Nov 26 to Dec 1, 2025, about six days. That's one snapshot, not the year's total. Most of 2025 just isn't in these datasets, so the real number was almost certainly much higher.
- **The current feed:** none of its rows mention 2025, while the same filter matches all 2,084 rows for 2026, so the search itself works. Its dates are stored as plain text, so I could only match on the year written in them. It also isn't confirmed whether each row is one report.

For a true full-year 2025 total, you'd need to ask the City and County of Honolulu directly, since their 311 system has records that aren't on the open data portal. I can also look at those 133 November reports by request type, status or ZIP code.

eval_answers.answer:
I can't answer this from Honolulu's open data. None of its 311 datasets records whether a report came in by phone or through the app.

I checked all three 311 datasets on the City and County of Honolulu portal (data.honolulu.gov):

| Dataset | Coverage | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| **HNL 311 Reports** (`jdy7-ftwe`) | 2,084 reports, Sept–Oct 2026 | id, date created, request type, street, city, state, ZIP, status, description |
| **Honolulu 311 Reports** (`6hui-dvrh`) | 133 reports, Nov 26 – Dec 1, 2025 | id, created/updated dates, request type, city, ZIP, location, status, description |
| **Honolulu 311 archive** (`pxs8-ci86`) | 24,375 reports, 2011–2019 | id, report type, status, description, created/closed dates, location |

None of them has a source, channel or intake-method field. Guessing the channel from the free-text descriptions wouldn't be reliable, so I haven't given numbers.

You could get the figures in two ways:
- **Ask the city directly.** Honolulu's Department of Customer Services runs 311, and its internal system probably tracks the channel. A records request or an email to the open-data team could get it.
- **Look for published reports.** The city's 311 annual reports or press releases sometimes give app versus phone percentages.

I can break the 311 data down by request type, status, ZIP code or date range instead.
